title: The night nightly_fin_load finished late
setting: Brindlecomb Wholesale, a fictional food-service distributor, runs a cloud data warehouse on the shared tier of a fictional provider, Corvane Cloud Data. Its nightly batch job, nightly_fin_load, starts at 01:30 UTC, extracts the day's orders, merges them into the staging table stage_orders, then builds 14 reporting models (marts) that feed the finance margin dashboards. The job must finish by 06:00 UTC; a deadline check then marks dashboards 'load incomplete' and pages on-call. The run of Thursday 22 October 2026 finished at 07:02 UTC. All times are UTC.
presentingRequest: The VP of Data & Analytics has asked Platform Reliability to confirm why the 22 October run missed its window and to sign off on corrective actions today. He has proposed his own explanation and three actions, and wants an answer before approving any changes.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Hollis Grange, VP Data & Analytics, to Platform Reliability, 22 Oct 08:12
initialEvidence.text: Subject: Last night's load. nightly_fin_load finished at 07:02, an hour past the 06:00 window. That's our first miss this year. Corvane posted a performance incident on our region overnight (we're on their shared tier), and we added customer_ltv to the job last week, so my read is platform trouble on top of extra load. I want to move us to the next Corvane tier, pull customer_ltv out of the job until it's proven safe, and switch off the 'load incomplete' banner, because the CFO saw it at 06:58 and thought the numbers were broken. Please confirm the diagnosis today so I can sign these off.

initialEvidence.source: Job telemetry summary, nightly_fin_load runs 22 Sep–21 Oct (30 runs)
initialEvidence.text: Total runtime: median 3h10m, range 2h52m–3h41m; latest finish 05:11. No lock waits over 2 minutes in any run. Monday-morning runs (4; they load Saturday and Sunday orders): mean 3h34m, mean 5.6M rows extracted. Other runs: mean 3h06m, mean 3.9M rows. The weekly storage snapshot runs Mondays 02:00–02:40. customer_ltv joined build_marts from the 15 Oct run: 17–21 min per run across 7 runs; total runtime median 3h08m before, 3h13m after. 22 Oct run: 4.08M rows extracted (Thursday median 4.01M); customer_ltv took 19m.

initialEvidence.source: Corvane public status page, incident CV-8812
initialEvidence.text: CV-8812 (Resolved). Degraded query performance, shared-tier clusters, eu-west region. Began 02:52 UTC, resolved 03:37 UTC, 22 Oct. Customers may have seen higher latency for queries submitted during this period. Dedicated-tier clusters were not affected. Cause: storage-node rebalancing following a hardware replacement. No data loss. We apologise for the inconvenience.

initialEvidence.source: Interview note, Amara Szell, Finance Reporting Lead, 22 Oct 10:30
initialEvidence.text: 'The banner went up at 06:00 saying today's load was incomplete and figures were as of 21 October. It's the only reason we didn't put Wednesday's margins into the 07:30 flash pack as Thursday's. We held the pack and sent it at 07:25 once the load had finished. The CFO asked about the banner and was fine once we explained. Separately, the retention team builds its 08:00 call list from customer_ltv every morning. When the model was missing during testing on 9 October they couldn't run their calls that day.'

catalogue.title: Corvane post-incident report for CV-8812
catalogue.text: Storage-node rebalancing in eu-west shared tier, 02:52–03:37 UTC on 22 Oct. Queries submitted during the window saw median latency up 22% and p95 up 41%. Statements already running at the start of the window saw little impact, as their data blocks were already cached on compute nodes. No queries failed. Remediation: rebalancing will now be throttled outside customer peak hours.

catalogue.title: Backfill script q3_restate.sh and its repository history
catalogue.text: q3_restate.sh: opens one session and runs a single UPDATE on stage_orders inside one transaction; no batching, no lock timeout set. Commits: 16 Oct 'q3 restate dry-run tweaks'; 20 Oct 16:58 'q3 restate: final'. README: 'Run via at(1) on analytics-host-2.' No cron or scheduler entry exists in the repository. Platform note: the at queue on analytics-host-2 is not retained after a job runs.

catalogue.title: Interview with the change board chair, 23 Oct
catalogue.source: Interview note, R. Okafor-Lind, Change Board chair
catalogue.text: 'We approved CHG-3317 for 13:00 Thursday. Our checklist for warehouse changes asks for a business stakeholder but not the owner of any batch job using the same tables, so nobody from the nightly side saw it. I didn't spot the 1:00 note. I can't tell you whether Varga meant one in the afternoon or one in the morning. People write it both ways, and Varga's last backfill was approved for overnight.'

catalogue.title: Storage snapshot schedule and run log, Sept–Oct
catalogue.text: Policy 'weekly-full': Mondays 02:00 UTC, full-cluster snapshot. Runs: 28 Sep 02:00–02:39, 5 Oct 02:00–02:41, 12 Oct 02:00–02:37, 19 Oct 02:00–02:38. All completed successfully. No snapshot scheduled or run on 22 Oct. No change to the policy since March.

catalogue.title: Corvane service agreement and SLA schedule
catalogue.text: Brindlecomb subscribes to Corvane shared tier, eu-west, 3-year term from February 2025. SLA: 99.5% monthly availability; service credits apply to unavailability only, not to performance degradation. Next tier ('dedicated'): about 2.3× current monthly cost, 30-day migration lead time. No credits were claimed in 2026.

hypotheses.text: The 22 Oct overrun was caused by the Q3 restatement backfill (pid 48812) holding an exclusive lock on stage_orders, which blocked the nightly merge step for over two hours.
Growth in order data volume pushed the 22 Oct run beyond its window.
Adding the customer_ltv model to the nightly job slowed the 22 Oct run enough to cause the overrun.
Corvane's regional performance incident (CV-8812) caused the 22 Oct overrun.
The backfill ran overnight because the implementer meant 13:00 but scheduled or wrote the start as '1:00', and did not deliberately choose an overnight run.

actions.text: Make the nightly_fin_load owner a mandatory reviewer for any change that writes to tables the job uses, bar such writes between 01:00 and 06:00 unless that owner signs off, and add an alert when a nightly step waits on a lock for more than 15 minutes.
Record a disciplinary finding against D. Varga for running the backfill outside its approved window.
Remove customer_ltv from the nightly job until it is proven safe.
Switch off the 'load incomplete' banner on the finance dashboards.
